title: Assembling the studio and road bands
summary: Players recruited from Miller, Dorsey and McKinley bands, and road auditions.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: How did you put the band together, as far as the people you had from the studio days? Were they people that you knew?
Oh, yeah. Some of them we didn't, but most of them we did and most of those we didn't we got through recommendation, as with Rosie and Buster; we knew Don.

Yes, and Trigger Alpert (phonetic spelling) had been with Bill Miller's band. Al Klink, Sid Cooper were Miller and Dorsey from Bill's band, and Nick and Joe Ferrante and Bobby Nichols from Dorsey. Nick and Joe Ferrante from McKinley's band. Vern Friley from McKinley's band.
In those times we never used tuba or bass trombone. We had Bill Barber the first time on tuba, because he had been with--we heard him with Gil's thing with Miles.
The Birth of the Cool record.
That was the road band. We spent weeks with auditions at Carol's studio and we got Harvey Estrom

there and Al Block and Ray Sheiner, Wally King--God bless Wally, Gene Allen; good players. Sonny Russo--we almost didn't get Sonny. Tommy Mitchell wanted to come as a B flat trombonist, wound up being one of the best bass trombonists in the country.
Nick came on the road with us, Bobby did; Joe couldn't--didn't want to, so we had Al Majorca (phonetic spelling) then.
